fieldMarks: Curving teardrop topknot on the head.
Male: reddish cap and a black patch in the centre of a yellowish belly.
Female: redder on the sides than a female California quail, with a less scaly belly pattern.
behavior: Coveys walk to water in the morning and evening, giving clucking and crowing notes; call is a ringing 'puk-kwaw-cah'.
Forages in flocks from late summer to early spring, mostly on the ground but also in shrubs for berries, leaves and buds.
Coveys roost at night in bushes or low trees.
Mostly vegetarian: seeds, shoots, leaves, cactus fruit and berries such as mistletoe and hackberry.
habitat: Brushy Sonoran desert and canyons with open ground, varied shrubs, cactus and mesquite thickets, concentrated near water. Avoids unbroken grassland without shrubs; can be common in open suburbs.
range: Desert Southwest of the United States, centred on the Sonoran Desert. Not found in Canada.

lookalikes.name: California quail
lookalikes.howToTell: The female Gambel's quail is redder on the sides with a less scaly belly than the female California quail.
